references.text: The parallel passage in Mark where the crowd reacts with amazement and asks one another: "What is this? A new teaching with authority! He even commands the unclean spirits, and they obey him." Almost identical reaction and wording.

Shortly before this verse, it is mentioned that the people were struck with wonder at Jesus' teaching because his words were spoken with authority (ἐξουσία). Verse 36 builds on this reaction following the specific exorcism.

The people's reaction to Jesus' teaching in the Sermon on the Mount – they were amazed at his teaching, for he taught them as one who has authority (ἐξουσία), and not as their scribes. The same theme of Jesus' authority that provokes amazement.
People wonder after Jesus calms the storm and ask: "What kind of man is this, that even wind and sea obey him?" The same pattern of amazement and questions about Jesus' identity and power.

The people in the synagogue at Capernaum were amazed at Jesus' teaching, for he taught them as one who has authority. The context is the same as in Luke 4, forming the background for the reaction in verse 36.

Jesus gives the twelve power (δύναμις) and authority (ἐξουσία) over all evil spirits. The same two words ἐξουσία and δύναμις are used here as in 4:36, showing that the authority the people saw was passed on to the disciples.

The seventy return with joy and say: "Lord, even the evil spirits submit to us in your name." Spiritual forces obey Jesus' name, just as the people in Capernaum testified that unclean spirits went out at his command.

Jesus rebukes the wind and says to the sea: "Be quiet!" – and the disciples ask: "Who is this?" Same pattern: Jesus commands with authority, and people respond with awe and questions about his identity.

Through Paul, God performed extraordinary miracles, so that diseases were healed and evil spirits went out. This shows that the power over unclean spirits that the people saw in Capernaum continued to work through the apostles.
